title: Strategy template
description: A model-agnostic algorithm: abstract roles, phases, review rules and completion semantics. Declarative on purpose — configuration never carries executable code.

roles.description: Abstract roles a playbook must bind to concrete participants.

writesCode.description: At most one role may set this. Within a run it is the sole writer to the workspace.

invokesOthers.description: Always false. The engine owns invocation, session ownership, ordering, budgets and cancellation; a coordinator influences others only by authoring handoff prompts.

requireCleanBase.description: Enforced at provisioning for base 'head': a checkout with tracked modifications refuses to start. Ignored for 'working-tree', whose whole point is a dirty checkout, and for an explicit commit.

base.description: What the worktree is cut from. 'head': the checked-out commit (refused when dirty and requireCleanBase). 'working-tree': a snapshot commit of the checkout as it is, tracked and untracked, symlinks included — for projects whose live state is not committed. { commit: <ref> }: an explicit ref. A playbook or a run may override; the choice and the resulting base commit are recorded on the run.

onUnsupported.description: Non-Git projects cannot be isolated. Default is to block rather than let an author loose on a live tree.

symlinks.description: What to do with symlinks in the worktree whose target resolves outside it. reject (default): refuse to provision and list them — a write through such a link changes a live file while the candidate's fingerprint records only the link. materialize: replace each with a copy of its target inside the worktree and re-snapshot, so the candidate is self-contained and the copy is the base. allow: keep them, record them on the run, and accept that writes through them are not captured.

tooling.description: What a participant's runtime may reach beyond the worktree and the run's scratch directory. Enforced by the adapters where the runtime allows (Claude: read/edit denied outside allowed roots through its permission settings, allowed roots added; Codex: a workspace-write sandbox rooted at the worktree), recorded on the run, and stated in the prompt. Bash cannot be path-fenced by either runtime; the recorded policy is what an auditor checks a transcript against.

allowLiveCheckout.description: May the runtime read the project's live checkout (the directory the worktree was cut from)? Default no: tooling loaded from there runs code outside the candidate.

allowedRoots.description: Additional absolute paths the runtime may read, e.g. a shared tooling directory. Never written.

mounts.description: Project setting only (projects/<id>.yaml; refused in a strategy or playbook). Host directories bind-mounted READ-ONLY into the seat fence at a worktree-relative path, so a seat can run the project's own tooling (its node_modules, a browser, a formatter install) without installing anything. Proved inside the fence before launch. A source that does not exist is not a configuration error: it resolves as missing (config:check --project warns) and every seat turn of that project is refused, naming the path. Mounted paths are left out of the snapshot, the fingerprint and the patch.

target.description: Where the directory appears, relative to the worktree root (e.g. gui/node_modules). Normalised, no '..', no '.git', not nested in another target.

source.description: The host directory: absolute, or relative to the project checkout. Inside the project's own checkout it must hold nothing the snapshot selects (dependency trees, not source).

provisional.description: The path is the configuration's best knowledge, not yet proved by a live tooling turn (npm run live -- --tooling).

commands.description: Project setting only. The commands a seat may use with the mounted tooling. Authors, auditors and the coordinator are given each one in the form the engine renders (cd <cwd> && /run/devpanel/tooling/offline sh -c '<run>'): it runs with no network, and a listed command is not 'could not run' unless the attempt and its output are quoted.

run.description: A shell command line, run by sh -c inside the network-isolated wrapper. <placeholders> are for the seat to fill in.

cwd.description: Worktree-relative working directory; the worktree root when absent.

substantial.description: Defines what counts as substantial — the thing that keeps a ping-pong loop going. Anything not matching is recorded but does not block.

protocolRepair.description: An unparseable or self-contradictory result is a protocol failure, not a review finding. Repair asks the same participant to restate in the required shape; it never routes work to the author.

onExhausted.description: The run enters blocked and waits for a human. It must never fall through to changes-needed.

concurrentReviews.description: Run the occupied reviewers of one consensus round at the same time (default true). Consensus is folded after all of them are recorded either way; false keeps them one after another.

checks.description: How much this strategy's conclusions depend on verification. This is POLICY only — whether checks can actually run is a runtime outcome, recorded as a result in run.json, and never feeds back into policy.

requirement.description: required: auto-close needs a passed result on the approved fingerprint; an unavailable target BLOCKS the run rather than downgrading. optional: a result, if there is one, must not be failed. none: checks play no part.

maxCostUsd.description: Ceiling on KNOWN cost in USD. Steps whose provider reports no price are counted separately and cannot be capped.

onExhausted.description: Budget exhaustion always leaves the issue unresolved.

retryPolicy.description: How a runtime failure classified as rate-limit, transient or output-limit is retried. Quota, credential and environment failures are never retried.

maxDelaySeconds.description: Cap on any wait (default 600). A provider's own retry-after is honoured within the cap.

action.description: Different completion points. 'none' produces a candidate and stops; the artifact remains under runs/<run-id>/artifacts/.

revalidateBeforeDelivery.description: Re-derive the fingerprint immediately before delivering. If integration changed the candidate, approval and checks are stale and must be renewed.

checksUnavailable.description: Requirement 'required' with no usable result. Never downgrades to unavailable-and-proceed.

closureNotAuthorised.description: Every condition met, but evidence is review-only and autoClose demands verified.

autoClose.description: Authority to close, which is separate from evidence. review-only describes what is known; it does not by itself authorise an automatic close.

minimumVerification.description: verified (default): auto-close requires a passed check bound to the closing fingerprint. review-only: auto-close is permitted on agreement alone — an explicit, deliberate opt-in, never a fallback the engine chooses.

contextRef.description: Named reference into run state. findings.plan is the substantial findings raised while the plan was under review, which an implementation reviewer must give a disposition for. plan.current is the latest plan the author produced (revisions included); plan.approved is the plan the approving audit examined, null until a plan review approves. steps.plan.response is only the first draft. {{previous.response}} is deliberately not expressible: a review usually needs the issue, the approved plan, the latest implementation response and the outstanding findings, which must be named individually.

id.description: Also the step folder slug. Slugs repeat across rounds; the number disambiguates.

prompt.description: Template file under prompts/, relative to the strategy directory. Mutually exclusive with promptFrom.

promptFrom.description: Use a prompt authored at runtime by another participant, e.g. steps.handoff-plan.output.prompt.

output.description: Which agent-output contract this turn must satisfy.

recordsRevision.description: After this turn the engine fingerprints the workspace and binds the result to the step.

concurrent.description: Only on a single-step phase: run at once with the consecutive single-step phases whose steps are also concurrent (the triage investigators). The loader refuses it on a step with transitions, a revision, a source-writing role, or one that reads another concurrent step's output.

access.description: Phase 1 of the seat-access fence (harness/README.md "Seat hygiene"): `read` lets a coordination-only turn read the run's source snapshot and run read-only commands inside the seat fence; `checks` lets it read the run's own check logs and evidence (not the source) the same way. Both stay tool-free when the fence cannot be proved or is off.

when.description: Run this phase only when the declarative guard holds over the run's resolved release plan, e.g. release.mode == staging-then-production. Absent, the phase always runs.

onExhausted.description: unresolved: round exhaustion blocks the run. await-input: the run pauses and the operator may answer `continue` (exactly one more round) or `stop`. extend-if-converging: no question; one extra round is granted when the last round left fewer substantial findings (a failed check counts as one) than the round before it and none of them reopens a finding id an earlier round of the loop closed, otherwise the run ends as unresolved.

to.description: A phase id, 'abort', 'ask-owner' (end the run after this step, unresolved, recording the triage output's autonomy questions or split for the issue owner; answering starts a fresh run), or 'await-input' (pause the run with `question` for the operator; the answer becomes `decisions` context and the run continues).

question.description: For to: await-input. May render {{output.<field>}} from the step's structured output.
